text: I will read a poem, when I pause you may recite back what I said as accurately as possible. After you recite it back, we will continue to the next verse, until the poem is finished.
The first poem is “Invention” by Billy Collins. Here we go!
Tonight the moon is a cracker,
nothing but stars in the sky, and I will have a few nights to myself, a little time to rest my jittery pen.
We will now recite another poem, called “The Moment” by Margaret Atwood
The moment when, after many years of hard work and a long voyage
We never belonged to you. You never found us. It was always the other way round.
We will now recite another poem, called “Stopping by woods on a snowy evening” by Robert Frost
Whose woods these are I think I know. His house is in the village though; He will not see me stopping here
The woods are lovely, dark and deep, But I have promises to keep, And miles to go before I sleep, And miles to go before I sleep.
Now we will continue to the next part of the experiment.
